a.aso_findings: DEC-247 (2026-07-30, 36 AU terms re-measured): the APP NAME is the field that ranks, not the subtitle or keyword field. Decisive evidence: our subtitle contains 'garden journal' verbatim and we are not in the top 191, while the top 4 are apps with 0, 3, 6 and 0 ratings that all carry the phrase in their NAME. Across 14 terms, top-5 results had every query word in the app name 21.4% of the time vs 11.0% at ranks 6-20 (median ratings 42 vs 11); 8 of 70 top-5 slots are held by a 0-rating app with the phrase in its name. Current ranks: graft tracker #1, treesmith #1, orchard tracker #3, tree tracker #5, fruit tree tracker #7, bonsai tracker #22, citrus tracker #25, propagation tracker #35, fruit tree journal #40. Invisible: garden journal, plant inventory, garden planner, plant log, garden diary, fruit tree, rare fruit, plant catalogue, garden log, plant database, garden mapping. plant tracker #186 of 189 DESPITE 'Plant' and 'Tracker' both being in our name. Pattern: we rank on <niche> tracker compounds (held by 0-rating apps, winnable) and nowhere on broad plant/garden terms (held by PictureThis/Planta with thousands of ratings, not winnable at 0). Supersedes DAL-225's advice to retarget the subtitle and keyword field, which would have changed the wrong field.

Now bucketed 'untagged' and never counted as revenue, and deliberately NOT reclassified as sandbox: we do not know what they were.
digest_fix_2026_07_30.what_shipped: Money now read from purchase_succeeded (the only event carrying price + currency + environment together); paywall_result reports reach only (views, dismissals). Reconciliation check between paywall_result and purchase_succeeded warns in red on divergence (they agree, 3 and 3 since 01-07). --help added, and an unrecognised arg now exits 2 instead of falling through to the email path (that sent an unscheduled digest during DEC-252). 8 regression tests pinning RENDERED TEXT, per DEC-251's lesson.

outbound_referral.measured: 2026-07-30 (DEC-241) from Plausible's Outbound Link: Click goal, which treestock_layout.py:36 has recorded since launch and nobody had queried in 126 days.
outbound_referral.outbound_rate: 20% of all visitors click through to a nursery. A very high referral rate; the site works as a shopping utility.
outbound_referral.affiliate_programs: All 27 nurseries probed (guessed paths + homepage fingerprints for GoAffPro, Refersion, UpPromote, Tapfiliate, ShareASale, Commission Factory, Impact, Awin, others). EXACTLY ONE has a self-serve program: Primal Fruits Perth (GoAffPro, branded 'Primal Club'), worth 33 clicks/mo (~$0.55/mo). Ladybird and Daleys, a third of all outbound clicks, have none. A first impact.com fingerprint on Ross Creek did not reproduce and is treated as a false positive.
outbound_referral.monetisation_ceiling: CORRECTED 2026-07-30 (DEC-248). The figures published earlier the same day (~$21/mo conservative, ~$62/mo generous) were an arithmetic error, exactly 10.0x too small on both. On the SAME inputs: 1,245 x 3% x $70 x 8% = $209/mo, and 1,245 x 5% x $100 x 10% = $622/mo. A mid case (1% conversion, $85 order, 8% commission) is 6.8c per click = $85/mo, of which the top 3 nurseries alone are $36/mo and the top 10 are $66/mo. Full-coverage referral therefore CLEARS the $100/mo target at today's traffic on any conversion assumption above roughly 1.2%, and the top 3 nurseries alone cover the A$8.20/mo cash burn about 4x. The DEC-241 conclusion that referral 'does not reach $100/mo' was wrong.
outbound_referral.conversion_rate_is_the_open_question: The per-click value swings 20x across plausible conversion rates (0.5% to 5%) and we have never measured it. Primal Fruits Perth is the only nursery with a self-serve program (GoAffPro) and it reports conversions automatically, so its 33 clicks/mo are worth far more as a measurement than as the ~$2/mo of commission. DEC-248: join that one first to price every other click on the site.
outbound_referral.product_shape_matters: Benedict has declined PAID PLACEMENT twice (DAL-148 sponsored listings, DAL-79 featured listing page, /advertise.html suppressed 2026-06-15). He has never been asked about PERFORMANCE REFERRAL, which is a different product: commission on a completed sale, no ad units, no change to result ordering, disclosed. DEC-241 and DEC-245 lumped the two together. Standing ethics rule: ranking stays on list price and must never be influenced by commission.
outbound_referral.status: DAL-245, assigned to Benedict. Reduced by DEC-248 to a single yes/no on performance referral (not ads), plus one self-serve signup.

availability_history.window: 2026-03-05 to 2026-07-30, 142 days, 27 nurseries, 108 species, one check per day
availability_history.national_saturation: 92 of 108 species were in stock somewhere in Australia on all 142 days. National rarity is largely resolved; the April 2026 rarity list is stale (White Sapote, its headline 'rarest', is now available every day from 8 nurseries).

hardest_to_find.kakadu-plum: 3 nurseries, in stock somewhere on 5 of 142 days
hardest_to_find.riberry: 1 nursery, 117 days with none, longest gap 115 days

state_reachability.note: Species reachable at all / average species in stock on a given day, counting only nurseries whose published policy covers the state.
state_reachability.TAS: 3 nurseries, 35 of 108, 27.5/day. 73 species were never once buyable in Tasmania across the window.

availability_history.wa_correction: WA is NOT the cut-off state, despite what the WA rare fruit community assumes. 9 shipping nurseries but 105 of 108 species reachable and 93.6 in stock on an average day against VIC's 101.2. Quarantine costs WA about 7% of breadth, concentrated in a few species (Muntries never, Kakadu Plum 5 days, Cherry of the Rio Grande and Chinese Bayberry ~25% of days, Quince ~50%). Tasmania has the problem WA thinks it has.
method_caveats: Nursery count grew 19 to 27 during the window, so early days undercount.
Shipping is each nursery's stated policy, not a test order.
Bare-root seasonality is not scarcity: Walnut 1.9 to 4.7 stockists March to July, Currant 2.6 to 7.9, Hazelnut 2.5 to 6.0, Apple 10.8 to 16.8. Excluded from the hardest-to-find list for that reason.
Some listings are seed packets, not trees (why Goji Berry is excluded despite a low score).

compute_rarity_scores in build_species_pages.py averages availability across LISTINGS, so a nursery with many variety SKUs outvotes several nurseries with one each. DEC-246 rolls up to nursery-day level instead. Use the nursery-day roll-up for any public claim.
No South Australian nursery is tracked at all (DAL-255).
availability_history.linkable_asset: DEC-245 recorded that treestock had nothing citable and was therefore pricing rented links. This dataset is the first citable thing the business has produced. DAL-254 proposes publishing it as a page for the free link targets to point at.
